paper: Arithmetic and harmonic realizations of the Clebsch cubic

integral_boundary.geometric_incidence_comparison: over Z[1/N] for an unspecified nonzero N divisible by 2, 3, and 5
integral_boundary.mod_11_scope: good reduction of the explicit golden fibre and exchanger, with no matching-sheet identification and no global integral incidence comparison

claims.statement: Over Q, Hitchin's icosahedral incidence extension has equation w^2=5J0, and J0 restricts to 16 sigma3^2 on the Clebsch chart.
The fibre over xyz consists of two conjugate golden configurations, and their exchanger reduces modulo 11 with nontrivial spinor class.

The ten explicitly labelled face-axis zonal harmonics embed the 1+4+5 permutation module into H_6, with normalized spherical Gram matrix one thirteenth of the reproducing kernel and the Clebsch four-space equal to the Petersen minus-two eigenspace.
The normalized degree-six spherical cubic restricts to -784000/1247103 times sigma3 on the Clebsch four-space.

boundaries: The arithmetic and harmonic theorems share the Clebsch four-space and the polynomial sigma3; no canonical or integral comparison between the two constructions is claimed.
The checker validates structure and ledger consistency; it does not certify mathematical truth.
The harmonic bundle distinguishes the reproducing kernel from the normalized spherical Gram matrix and independently replays the exact moments.
The abstract quadratic algebra is finite etale over D(10J), but comparison with the geometric incidence model is proved only over Z[1/N] for an unspecified N.
The rational 5-twist normalizes Hitchin's known degree-two incidence cover; Dye already proves the square-5 field criterion for Clebsch hexagons.
